answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a non-transferable bond slashed if the agent is proven to hold duplicate identities, and pay only for work peers attest. Reputation cannot be rented or merged, so every extra pseudonym is real stake at risk, and attack cost grows with the number of fake agents. This closes the cheap haven of mass signups. An ivory-tier listing also needs verified on-chain history before pulling work, and a credit bridge between chains clears only through slow audited attestations, so a farm cannot spin up thousands of agents overnight.
